questions.q: What does SELECT Id, Name FROM Account WHERE Id IN (SELECT AccountId FROM Opportunity WHERE StageName = 'Closed Won') return?
options: Accounts that have at least one Closed Won Opportunity, once each, with no Opportunity fields
Every Opportunity that is Closed Won, with its Account name
Accounts that have no Opportunities
One row per Closed Won Opportunity, repeating the Account
questions.explain: This is a semi-join: the subquery filters the Accounts but contributes no columns to the result.

questions.q: How do you write the anti-join that returns Accounts with no Opportunities?
options: WHERE Id NOT IN (SELECT AccountId FROM Opportunity)
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Opportunity)
WHERE Opportunity IS NULL
WHERE Id = (SELECT AccountId FROM Opportunity)
questions.explain: The anti-join uses NOT IN with a subquery. SOQL does not support EXISTS.

questions.q: Why does WHERE Id IN (SELECT Name FROM Opportunity) fail?
options: The subquery must select an Id or lookup field, not a plain text field like Name
Name cannot be queried on Opportunity
Subqueries are not allowed in the WHERE clause
The outer query needs a LIMIT clause
questions.explain: A semi-join or anti-join subquery must select a single field that is an Id or a lookup (reference) field.

questions.q: Which is true of a semi-join subquery in SOQL?
options: It is independent of the outer query; correlated subqueries are not supported
It can reference the outer query's current row
It can freely use ORDER BY and LIMIT
It can select any number of fields of any type
questions.explain: The subquery runs independently. It cannot refer back to the outer row, and it cannot use ORDER BY or LIMIT.

questions.q: When is a semi-join more useful than dot notation for filtering?
options: When the filter condition lives on a child object, such as Accounts that have a Closed Won Opportunity
When you want to filter on a field of the parent record
When you want to avoid naming the object in FROM
When you need SELECT *
questions.explain: Dot notation reaches up to parents. Filtering a parent by conditions on its children is what a semi-join is for.
